clue.text: Student boarding at university that man had sustained

parts.note: being up means being in residence at a university

indicators.note: someone boarding gets on and sits inside a vehicle, so the student is placed within the other letters

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had
L is a learner, the plate shown by a student driver

explanation.surface: A student lodging at college has been supported by some man.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at a university is the British phrase for being in residence there, as in up at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold something is to support or maintain it, so upheld and sustained are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Change name into name

indicators.note: to change these letters is to swap them about into a fresh order

parts.note: the first two words taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter one's name into another name.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first 'name' together with 'into'; the final 'name' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put forward or appoint them by stating who they are, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Designed and erected right at the heart of things

definitions.text: right at the heart of things

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are planned out and constructed in a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A building planned and put up at the very hub of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead centre means the exact middle point, exactly where something lies at its core.

clue.text: Supermodel that wouldn't be attracted to Mick Jagger?

definitions.text: Supermodel that wouldn't be attracted to Mick Jagger?

parts.note: surface reading: a famous fashion model who has no interest in the rock singer

parts.words: wouldn't be attracted to Mick Jagger
parts.note: setter's reading: the proverb says a rolling stone gathers none of this plant, and Jagger is a Rolling Stone

explanation.walkthrough: Kate Moss is the supermodel; the proverb 'A rolling stone gathers no moss' supplies the joke, since Jagger fronts the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is a famous British supermodel, and moss is the plant a rolling stone proverbially never gathers.

clue.text: Do something resulting in penalty and away goal

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football picture: a foul conceded and a goal scored on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to commit an offence, a breach of rules that brings a punishment.

clue.text: National clubs wearing such flimsy kit would show carelessness

indicators.note: when the abbreviations are worn inside the answer you get the longer word, so removing them from that word leaves the garment

parts.note: neglect or lack of proper care
N is the abbreviation for national
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A national team in see-through shirts would look sloppy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: N and C worn inside NEGLIGEE make NEGLIGENCE, so take them out of the longer word to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, sheer nightgown, flimsy clothing that the clue calls kit.

clue.text: Object to half-naked model

indicators.note: only half of the next word survives, the rest being dropped

parts.note: naked can mean open or uncovered, as a naked flame
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Objecting to a model posing half-undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to resist or argue against it, so it works as a verb phrase swap.

clue.text: Missing every penalty, just like the England team?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, free of Scottish players

explanation.surface: England fail to score a single spot kick, a familiar football lament.
explanation.walkthrough: Missing a penalty sounds like a footballer's miss, but it means avoiding punishment; an England side contains no Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping without punishment; scot was an old tax or payment.

clue.text: Way accent limits Essex town's means of progressing

indicators.note: something that limits another bounds it on either side, so these letters enclose the next ones

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
tone of voice is a manner of speaking
Epping is a town in Essex, a county east of London; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Local speech constraining what a town in Essex can do.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'town's' is kept as a letter S, not just possessive grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is a stage that helps someone advance towards a goal, figuratively a way forward.

clue.text: Once again inspire some more kind leaders

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Encouraging kinder leaders to motivate people anew.
explanation.definitionFit: To rekindle is to light again, figuratively to revive feelings or enthusiasm anew.

clue.text: See team play regularly to get fit

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Watch the side train often to improve your fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like physical fitness, but here it means suitable or proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper or appropriate, the sense of fit in 'fit for the occasion'.

clue.text: Sensitive director initially stops programme targeting consumers?

indicators.note: to stop something can mean to plug a gap in it, sitting inside like a stopper

parts.note: being aware is being conscious or sensitive to something

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A thoughtful director halts a show aimed at shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: D is plugged into AWARE: A(D)WARE. A programme here is software, and the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adware is software that shows advertisements to computer users, so it aims at people as buyers.

clue.text: Example showing name-dropping male

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the letter standing for that word is removed

parts.note: parading is showing off or displaying
N is the abbreviation for name
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man who drops famous names, held up as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: PARADING loses its N, then M is added: PARADIG + M.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical model or pattern of something, a standard instance.

clue.text: Revival related to certain implicating information on conservative

indicators.note: to implicate is to involve or draw in, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: re means concerning or about
sure means certain
gen is British slang for information
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A comeback tied to a certain leak of damaging information about a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, then SURE holding GEN, then C below it in this down answer: RE + SUR(GEN)E + C.
explanation.definitionFit: A resurgence is a rise again after a decline, so revival is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cruel person, because of what has gone before, returns

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.words: because of what has gone before
parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, drawing a conclusion from what precedes

explanation.surface: A tyrant comes back because of past events.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folk tales, and by extension any brutal or frightening person.

clue.text: Spherical ball most of group kicked around

indicators.note: something kicked around is knocked about in all directions, so these letters are scattered
most of means nearly all, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A round football passed about by a bunch of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Globular means shaped like a globe, round like a ball, so it matches the adjective exactly.

clue.text: What may manipulate Barnet's Chinese communities?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tools for curling hair; Barnet, short for Barnet Fair, is rhyming slang for hair
second meaning: Chinese secret societies or associations

explanation.surface: Something that could influence the Chinese residents of Barnet, a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but it is rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair; curling tongs style it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are gripping tools, including curling irons for hair, and tongs are also Chinese secret fraternal societies.

clue.text: A part of the Far East

indicators.note: part of means just a piece of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A region of eastern Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' looks like the article, but it is the definition: A is the standard abbreviation for area, as on maps and in formulae.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is a recognised short form for area, as in the formula A equals length times width.

clue.text: Rebuke handsome man embracing married husband

indicators.note: embracing means holding in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth
M is the abbreviation for married
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Telling off a good-looking man who is hugging a wedded husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprimand or warn firmly, the same verb sense as to scold.

clue.text: Virtue that is unexpected

definitions.note: describes the use of the answer as an exclamation of surprise
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an exclamation of surprise, as in 'My ...!'

explanation.surface: Good behaviour that comes as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodness is moral rectitude, and the word also serves as a mild oath voiced on being surprised.

clue.text: Stupid Australian bird with a taste for cricket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Australian slang for a fool

definitions.text: bird with a taste for cricket?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an insect-eating songbird, cricket being the insect not the sport

explanation.surface: A dim Aussie fan with a passion for cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket suggests the Australian sport, but the bird eats the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a drongo is an idiot, and drongos are black songbirds that feed on insects.

clue.text: Note what teachers involved in dispute might do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a comment or observation

definitions.text: what teachers involved in dispute might do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., to grade work again after an appeal

explanation.surface: An observation about teachers in an industrial dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: A dispute sounds like a strike, but it is a challenged grade that teachers would mark again.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a comment, and to re-mark is to assess pupils' work a second time.

clue.text: Noise made by bat

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the strung implement used in tennis or squash

explanation.surface: A sound produced by a bat, the animal or a cricket bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud uproar, and also the stringed frame used to hit a ball in tennis.

clue.text: Boat in which you're unlikely to see skipper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a canoe made from a hollowed log

definitions.text: in which you're unlikely to see skipper?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the touchline shelter for managers and substitutes, while the team captain is out on the pitch

explanation.surface: A vessel that seems to sail without its captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipper looks like a boat's captain, but it is the team captain, who plays rather than sits in the shelter by the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a hollowed-log canoe and also the sunken bench area beside a football pitch.

clue.text: What lead tense husband and wife to relax?

indicators.note: what leads these words is their opening letters, taken in turn

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: What could get an uptight married couple to unwind?
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw is to become less frosty or more friendly, loosening up like melting ice.

clue.text: Old king occupying Italian city is too picky

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: an occupier lives inside a place, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Venice is the canal city of Italy
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch living in an Italian city is fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for rex, Latin for king, as in royal cyphers like ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnice means excessively fastidious or particular, so fussy to a fault.

clue.text: Four-letter words in English?

parts.note: surface reading: short English words of four letters
setter's reading: swearing, as in 'mind your ...', and English is itself an example of one

explanation.walkthrough: Four-letter words are swear words, which people call bad language; English is also a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tongue such as English, and also crude speech, as in bad language.

clue.text: Company's delivered classes for religious people

indicators.note: delivered as in a speech delivered, so the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a cast is a theatre company; with 's it is pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: A firm providing lessons for the devout.
explanation.walkthrough: Company is a theatrical cast, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Castes are hereditary social classes, most famously the divisions within Hindu society.
